ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows five straight lines meeting at one common central point, creating ten rays around that point. Five triangles are drawn around the center, each triangle having its vertex at the common intersection point. In each of the five triangles, the two outer/non-central angles are marked with arcs, giving 10 marked angles total; the central angles of the triangles are unmarked. Reasoning: Let the five unmarked central angles inside the triangles have total C, and let the total of the 10 marked angles be M. For each triangle, its two marked angles plus its central angle sum to 180°. Summing over the five triangles gives M + C = 5 × 180° = 900°. Around the common point, the five central triangle angles are alternate sectors among the ten sectors formed by five concurrent straight lines. For an odd number of straight lines, these alternate sectors sum to 180°. Thus C = 180°, so M = 900° − 180° = 720°.

method.method_draft: Identify from the diagram that each of the five triangles has its vertex at the common intersection point, and the 10 marked angles are exactly the two non-central angles in these five triangles. Let the five unmarked central angles inside the triangles be the apex angles. For each triangle, the two marked angles plus its central apex angle sum to 180°, so the total of all 10 marked angles equals 5·180° minus the sum of the five central apex angles. Because the image and statement show five straight lines all passing through the same point, the 10 small angles around the point come in a cyclic sequence where the five triangle apex angles are alternate sectors. For an odd number of concurrent straight lines, these alternate sectors sum to 180°. Therefore the marked-angle total is 900° − 180° = 720°.
